 11/12 Preview – Kevin Fiala Set To Return + 22’s Impact, Managing Expectations, Doughty Expected To Play, “Kuemper’s 500
 By Zach Dooley 
 7 hours ago 
 328 Comments 
 Share This Article 
 Share This Article 
 WHO: Los Angeles Kings (5-9-2) vs. New York Islanders (7-6-4)
 WHAT: 2026-27 NHL Regular Season, Game 17/84
 WHEN: Thursday, November 12 @ 7:00 PM Pacific
 WHERE: Crypto.com Arena – Los Angeles, CA
HOW TO FOLLOW: VIDEO: ESPN+ / Hulu – VIDEO: 830 AM KLAA, ESPN LA App, LA Kings App – TWITTER: @dooleylak & @lakings 
 TODAY’S MATCHUP: With two games remaining on their current seven-game homestand, the Kings sit with a record of 2-3-0, in hopes of evening the slate. 
 HEAD-TO-HEAD: The Kings defeated the Islanders 3-2 when these teams met earlier this season. Forward Artemi Panarin led the way with two goals, while defenseman Brandt Clarke scored the game-winning goal in overtime, as a part of a multi-point effort. Goaltender Darcy Kuemper made a season-high 41 saves in the game to earn the win.
 KINGS VITALS: After a full-team practice yesterday, the Kings held an optional morning skate today at Toyota Sports Performance Center. 
 Goaltender Darcy Kuemper is expected to make the start tonight against the Islanders in what will be the 500th appearance of his NHL career. Kuemper is set to become the 87th goaltender in NHL history to reach 500 games played. The veteran netminder has a lifetime record of 11-6-2 versus New York, with a .916 save percentage and a 2.51 goals-against average. 
 Based on what we’ve seen over the last couple of days, as well as this morning’s skate, here is a projected lineup for tonight’s game – 
 Panarin – Laferriere – Kempe
Fiala – Byfield – Zuccarello
Moore – Laughton – Perry
Lee – Haula – Armia
 Anderson – Doughty
Edmundson – Clarke
Dumoulin – Ceci
 Forsberg
Kuemper
 Looks like tonight might be the night! The Kings are expected to get forward Kevin Fiala back in the lineup this evening against the Islanders. As far as other forwards, I’m not sure exactly who will be in, but it looked like Alex Turcotte and Samuel Helenius were both on late after today’s morning skate, which feels like a bit of a change from practice yesterday. Forward Kenny Connors was loaned to AHL-Ontario this morning, while defenseman Erik Gustafsson remains out of action on a day-to-day basis. 
 ISLANDERS VITALS: New York has lost its last four games entering tonight’s action, including a 3-2 shootout loss to begin its current three-game trip on Tuesday in San Jose. 
 Per Andrew Gross of Newsday, here’s how the Islanders lined up last time out versus the Sharks – 
 #Isles in warmups (Game No. 17 at #SJSharks) Holmstrom-Horvat-Palmieri Heineman-Schenn-Eklund Palat-Pageau-Duclair MacLean-Cizikas-Chaffee Pelech-Schaefer Stanley-DeAngelo Hutton-Kessel Sorokin Varlamov
 — Andrew Gross (@AGrossNewsday) November 10, 2026 
 Defenseman Matthew Schaefer leads the Islanders this season with 12 assists and is tied for the New York team lead with 17 total points. Schaefer’s five goals are tied for the sixth most in the NHL among defensemen, including a goal against Los Angeles when these teams met in October. 
 Storyline Of The Day – KEVIN! 
 Today’s the day! The LA Kings are expected to welcome forward Kevin Fiala back to the lineup tonight against the New York Islanders. 
 Fiala has been out of action for 46 LA Kings games. He missed the first 16 games of the 2026-27 regular season, in addition to all four in the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs and the final 26 of the 2025-26 regular season. In that time, Fiala has had two procedures, to help repair fractures in his left leg and get him back to full health, following an injury suffered at the 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan.
 In late-October, Fiala rejoined the Kings for practice, first in a non-contact jersey. He’s been with the team ever since, showing steady signs of progression. He wasn’t that far off from the timeline that Ken Holland spelled out nearly two months ago, with an early-November return to action now established. 
 In his first game, I would expect that we will see Fiala on a line with Mats Zuccarello and Quinton Byfield. It’s the winger-pairing that I think we all expected over the summer, with those two players forming a second scoring line, in support of the Artemi Panarin and Adrian Kempe pairing higher on the lineup. Two players who were teammates in Minnesota, players who were productive together in limited spurts, despite not always playing on the same forward line. While Byfield wasn’t the projected center there, Alex Laferriere’s fit on the first line makes him the natural third member of that trio.
 Here’s what his projected linemates had to say about his return – 
 Byfield – Everybody knows how good Kevin is and how much he means to us, not just on the ice, but in the locker room. Just being able to be on the ice with him, make plays with him, I’ve played with him for like two years and we’ve had some good chemistry. We read off each other, he likes to play off the rush and I do as well. If we can get that going, the interchange, the movement, with how much skill he has……I feel like it’s a lot of fun playing with him.
 Zuccarello – He’s a huge part of this group and has been one of the best players here for a long time. To have him back in, it’s obviously good for the team. We played together in Minnesota, we had some success there……he’s a smart player, he makes plays, he makes other people better. That’s I think the biggest compliment to him is he makes the people around him better and that’s what we need.
 I stand by what I wrote yesterday, in that to simply expect Fiala to come in and be a savior for a struggling team is unfair to him. He needs time to get up to speed, having not played a game in nine months, without a training camp to benefit him. That being said, it’s still very exciting to see a player of his caliber return to the lineup, especially right now, for a team in need of a spark. Fiala is a dynamic, offensive player and the Kings need to score more goals. Fiala helps in that area.
 I think that both things could be true. Fiala’s return is extremely exciting. We should also be tempering expectations and allowing him the time to settle in, re-establish his game and work his way back to full strength. Exciting nonetheless, though and it certainly makes tonight’s game an interesting one to watch. 
 3 To Watch For – 
– Regarding that balance between excitement and expectation, I posed that exact question to Peter Laviolette.
 “I think there’s something to that. He looks great in practice, but I think once you get into a game and it becomes live, it’s always a little bit of a different feel. To me, he looks like he’s confident, just in the way he practices and the way he moves on the ice in practice. I think it’s a good entry point for him. We’ll communicate with him through the game as it moves on.”
 Fiala hasn’t played a game in nine months. I think that Laviolette and the coaching staff have done a good job of tempering those expectations for a player who they know is important, but who has also been out of action. It’s important not to view Fiala as a savior for a struggling team. It’s also important to test him in game situations and see what he’s got, because he can help the team. 
 As he did with Zuccarello on Tuesday, Laviolette will be in constant communication with Fiala throughout the game, to see where he’s at. 
 “Kevin’s been on the ice for awhile now, his game, his conditioning, his ability truly looks good to me out there, but again, there will be communication between he and I tonight as to where that goes,” Laviolette added. “I do think managing that expectation, both of these guys are contributing offensive players and they’re going to want to come in and have an impact, especially with Kevin, who has been out for a while.”
 – On the blueline, the current expectation is that Drew Doughty will be able to play tonight. 
 Doughty blocked a very heavy shot from Steven Stamkos late in the loss against Nashville on Tuesday. He did play one additional shift in that game but that was it for his evening. Doughty didn’t practice yesterday, with Laviolette referring to the absence as a maintenance day. He added this morning that he “believes” Doughty will play tonight, which is encouraging.
 Laviolette said that the coaches are still working through the defensive pairings right now, part of which comes down to Doughty’s availability and where he’s at. The Kings had to shuffle the deck with Erik Gustafsson out of action on Tuesday, which broke up the successful pair of Gustafsson with Brandt Clarke. It also separated a pairing with Doughty and Joel Edmundson, which has been very effective as well (6 GF, 1 GA). There aren’t all that many options with only six, but it was the duo of Brian Dumoulin and Cody Ceci who were on the ice for both 5-on-5 goals against on Tuesday, and you have to wonder if the Kings might look to break up a pairing that has seen both players have more success with other partners. We’ll see where it goes tonight, beginning with Doughty’s availability. 
 – Lastly, congratulations to goaltender Darcy Kuemper on his 500th career game in the NHL!
 As noted at the top, only 86 goaltenders in league history have reached that accomplishment, with Kuemper set to become the 87th. Tonight will be Kuemper’s 130th game with the Kings organization, over his two stints here in Los Angeles, his most of the five organizations he’s spent time with throughout his career. 
 Here’s what Joel Edmundson, Kuemper’s teammate in a few different places, had to say on Kuemper’s milestone moment – 
 “I’m fired up for the game just for that,” defenseman Joel Edmundson said about Kuemper’s milestone. “I’ve played with him at World Championships back in 2018 and then obviously in Washington together, so we’ve been together for a long time and I’m very pumped for him. Actually, we go way back to WHL days, I played against him in the WHL. For him to get to 500, it’s huge. It’s huge accomplishment for him, his family, his wife and his boys. They’re great. They’re some of the leaders of this team and yeah, we’re definitely going to build around that for sure.”
 I’m sure he’s not alone in a lot of those sentiments. 
 Would expect a pre-game ceremony for Kuemper either on Saturday or early in the next homestand. Hope to have some intel on that either tonight or tomorrow, depending on where everything lands. Congratulations to Darcy Kuemper on a milestone you don’t see every day, from a goaltender who, as Laviolette phrased it, has blended a mix of “success and longevity” which is not always an easy thing to do. 
 Well, here we go. Kings versus Islanders with a win needed tonight to have a chance at a winning homestand on Saturday versus Calgary. Excited to see Kevin Fiala back in action and will be attentive to see how the group responds around him, now that he is back in action.
